correctness.rationale: The binary definition yields an exact bounded-composition count. For first zero run ell near floor(log_2 n), the forbidden pattern 10^(ell+1) has asymptotically Poisson occurrences: inclusion–exclusion h-th terms converge to x^h/h!, while initial-boundary events vanish. The uniform lower-tail estimate follows from independent blocks and a second-moment bound, and the upper tail is a geometric series. This proves the whole summed phase law; Burnside gives the necklace normalization. A Mellin/Fourier substitution gives Gamma coefficients and strict nonconstancy. Reproducible exhaustive checks cover lengths 1–16 only and support, but cannot prove, the infinite statement.

value.rationale: Gabrić–Sawada introduced the quasinecklace candidate superset to obtain constant-amortized colex generation but the proved overhead was only O(1). A closed, nonconstant phase function is a natural next-order invariant of that algorithmic candidate-to-output ratio; its exact mean and first Fourier harmonic identify a subtle digital-oscillation obstruction to an ordinary limit. The result is not a parameter rename, finite recomputation or mere complexity-class improvement.
